successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the County of Vermandois, annexed to the royal domain in 1213

ledger.x: 990: the County of Vermandois, with Saint-Quentin and Péronne, enters the record.

1183: after Elisabeth's death Philip II 'moved to seize the province of Vermandois on behalf of Elisabeth's sister, Eleonore'; Eleanor's page has Philip of Flanders refuse her the county and her appeal to the king.
1186: peace between Philip II and Philip of Flanders.
1191: Philip of Alsace dies at Acre on 1 August and Vermandois falls to Eleanor and the crown.
1213: Eleanor dies without children (19 or 21 June) and the county passes to Philip II.

wars.name: War over the Vermandois succession
wars.outcome: Philip II backed Eleanor against her brother-in-law Philip of Alsace after Elisabeth's death; the peace of 10 March 1186 ceded Vermandois to the king while Philip kept the title for life, and he held the land until his death in 1191.

certainty.note: A feudal county drawn from Cliopatria's outline; the cession of Péronne and the 'eastern Vermandois' of 1191 have no boundary on any page opened.
